text: Try and except let you handle errors gracefully without crashing.
Division by zero would normally crash, [shush] but we catch ZeroDivisionError.
Accessing an invalid list index raises IndexError, and we handle it here too.
Your program keeps running instead of stopping.
The exception object carries a helpful message, and the as keyword lets you capture it to print or log.
You can catch several exception types at once by grouping them in a tuple after except.
[sigh] Else runs only when the try block succeeds with no exception, and finally runs every single time — success or failure.
[sniff] Catching errors precisely is better than a bare except, which would silently swallow bugs you actually want to see.
That makes finally perfect for cleanup, like closing a file, [cough] regardless of what happened above.
And you're not limited to built-in errors — raise lets you throw your own, custom exception whenever your code hits an invalid state.
